source.title: Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
source.authors: Patrick Esser; S. Kulal; A. Blattmann; Rahim Entezari; J. M¨uller; Harry Saini; Yam Levi; Dominik Lorenz; Axel Sauer; Frederic Boesel; Dustin Podell; Tim Dockhorn; Zion English; Kyle Lacey; Alex Goodwin; Yannik Marek; Robin Rombach; Aircraft Stability

record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling measurements to image and video generation models and reports downstream image-generation evaluations.
record.gate_note: The study reports image and video validation-loss scaling and relationships between validation loss and image/video generation evaluations. It does not report language-model scaling results, fitted power-law exponents, or compute-optimal allocations.
record.test_reason: The study trains MM-DiT image and video models of several sizes and durations and reports validation-loss scaling (V5). It also relates validation loss and model depth to GenEval, T2I-CompBench and human preference (V6). This is a new setting, diffusion/rectified-flow generation rather than language-model pretraining.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also state that the scaling study reached 8B parameters and 5×10^22 FLOPs. They argue validation loss is a simple, general measure of performance, and they make no power-law claim beyond 'predictable scaling trends'.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales rectified-flow image and video generation models and reports validation loss and generation evaluations; it does not reproduce language-model scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: For the depth=38 image model, learning-rate adjustments at 3 × 10^5 steps were needed to prevent divergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger models lose less CLIP score when sampled with fewer steps and have shorter ODE path lengths (Table 6: 5/50-step drop 4.30% at depth 15 vs 2.71% at depth 38).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sampling efficiency of rectified-flow models improves with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: Flow models trained on a 16-channel autoencoder latent need more capacity to match 8-channel FID; the gap becomes negligible at depth 22 (Fig. 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The scaling curve of latent generative models depends on latent dimensionality.

record.problems: The scaling curves are presented in figures without numerical loss values, fitted exponents, or uncertainty estimates. The video scaling study is described as preliminary, and its reported FLOPs exclude image pretraining.

untested.parts: The power-law functional form (no fit or exponent is reported); repeated data; fine-tuning and transfer scaling laws.
Language-model downstream tasks; any quantitative predictive fit or correlation coefficient.
Not tested (no extrapolation from small runs).
Not tested. Architecture comparisons (Fig. 4) are not at matched parameter count. Width is tied to depth (hidden size 64·d).
Not tested (no comparison of fitting choices).

missing.what: GenEval subcategory scores across depths 18–38, which are non-monotonic in Colors, Position and Single object
FID versus model depth for 4-, 8- and 16-channel autoencoders, showing that scaling depends on the latent setup

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Evidence for V5/V6 is mostly figure-only (Fig. 8) with no fitted exponents, numeric losses or correlation coefficients. Depth=38 needed a learning-rate intervention to avoid divergence. The video FLOPs omit image pretraining, which complicates any compute-based comparison.

versions.untested_parts: The claim concerns language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
No prediction of larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs is reported.
No fixed-compute parameter/token allocation sweep or compute-optimal split is reported.
Architecture comparisons are not reported at fixed parameter count as a test of the effect of depth, width, or other architecture details.
The study examines image and video models but does not fit or establish the same power-law form, or test repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling.

Downstream predictability is evaluated for image/video generation metrics and human preferences, not language-model downstream tasks; no numerical predictive relationship or correlation coefficient is reported.
The study does not compare scaling-law fitting choices or test whether fitted exponents or curves depend on them.
